questions.question: As per the Union Budget 2025-26, what is the revised annual limit for TDS deduction on rent?
questions.questionHtml: As per the Union Budget 2025-26, what is the revised annual limit for TDS deduction on rent?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ₹6 lakh.

In News

  • The Union Budget 2025-26 introduced significant reforms in TDS (Tax Deducted at Source) and TCS (Tax Collected at Source) thresholds.
  • The annual limit for TDS on rent has been increased from ₹2.40 lakh to ₹6 lakh.

Key Points

  • The tax deduction limit on interest for senior citizens has been doubled from ₹50,000 to ₹1 lakh.
  • The annual limit for TDS on rent has been increased from ₹2.40 lakh to ₹6 lakh.
  • The TCS threshold on remittances under RBI’s Liberalized Remittance Scheme (LRS) has been raised from ₹7 lakh to ₹10 lakh.
  • Only TDS and not TCS will be levied on goods sale transactions.
  • The government aims to rationalize and simplify the TDS/TCS structure by reducing the number of tax rates and applicable thresholds.

Additional Information

  • Union Budget
    • A budget is an elaborate statement of the expenditure and income of the government for the given financial year, which begins on April 1 and ends on March 31.
    • The Constitution uses the term Annual Financial Statement instead of "Budget," as enshrined under Article 112 of the Constitution.
  • Tax Deducted at Source (TDS)
    • TDS is a system where tax is deducted at the source of income generation and deposited with the government.
    • It applies to salaries, rent, professional fees, and interest income.
  • Tax Collected at Source (TCS)
    • TCS is the tax collected by a seller at the time of sale of certain goods or services.
    • Unlike TDS, which applies to payments, TCS applies to transactions like foreign remittances and specific high-value purchases.
  • Liberalized Remittance Scheme (LRS)
    • Under RBI’s LRS, individuals can send money abroad for travel, education, medical treatment, and investments.
    • The TCS threshold on remittances under LRS has been raised from ₹7 lakh to ₹10 lakh in the Union Budget 2025-26.

questions.question: The Pralay missile, whose salvo launch was recently conducted as part of user evaluation trials, is best described as which type of missile system?
questions.questionHtml: The Pralay missile, whose salvo launch was recently conducted as part of user evaluation trials, is best described as which type of missile system?

options.text: Intercontinental ballistic missile with nuclear warhead
options.html: Intercontinental ballistic missile with nuclear warhead

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Indigenously developed solid-propellant quasi-ballistic missile.

In News

  • DRDO successfully conducted a salvo launch of two Pralay missiles off the coast of Odisha as part of user evaluation trials.

Key Points

  • Pralay is an indigenously developed, solid-fuel, quasi-ballistic tactical missile.
  • Both missiles followed the intended trajectory and met all mission objectives.
  • The trials were monitored by tracking sensors of the Integrated Test Range, Chandipur.
  • The missile is intended for induction into the Indian Army and the Indian Air Force with conventional warheads.

Additional Information

  • Quasi-Ballistic Missile
    • Follows a lower and flatter trajectory than traditional ballistic missiles.
    • Capable of manoeuvring during flight to evade missile defence systems.
    • Combines features of ballistic flight with limited in-flight course correction.
  • Pralay Missile
    • First tested in December 2021.
    • Employs advanced guidance and navigation systems for high precision.
    • Can carry different types of conventional warheads against diverse targets.
  • Development Agencies
    • Developed by DRDO’s Research Centre Imarat, Hyderabad.
    • Supported by multiple laboratories including ARDE, HEMRL and R&DE (Engineers).
    • Industry partners include Bharat Dynamics Limited and Bharat Electronics Limited.

2. Tuhin Kanta Pandey has been recently appointed as the 11th SEBI Chairperson.

questions.question: Who is considered the father of Biology?
questions.questionHtml: Who is considered the father of Biology?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Aristotle.

Key Points

  • Aristotle -
    • The 'father of biology' is called the Greek philosopher Aristotle (384–322 BCE).
    • Aristotle arranged it with his ideas and concepts about biology.
    • Aristotle is also called the 'Father of Zoology' which is the branch of biology.
    • He was a disciple of Plato and a master of Alexander.
    • Aristotle's famous book on politics is "Politics".​

Additional Information

  • ​Theophrastus -
    • Theophrastus is the father of Botany.
    • Plants are studied in botany.
  • Carl Linnaeus-
    • He was a Swedish Botanist, Physician, and Zoologist.
    • Linnaeus made the first systematic attempt to classify Flora and Fauna.
    • Carl Linnaeus conceptualized the binomial nomenclature of classification.
  • ​Gregor John Mendel-
    • He was a German-speaking Austrian Augustinian pastor and scientist.
    • He is called the 'Father of Genetics.
    • He set the rules of genetics by experimenting on the seeds of peas.

Important Points

  • Mendel's three rules of genetics-
    1. Law of Dominance
    2. Law of Segregation
    3. Law of Independent Assortment

questions.question: Who among the following Hindustani classical musicians was NOT associated with ‘Maihar Gharana’?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following Hindustani classical musicians was NOT associated with ‘Maihar Gharana’?
questions.solution: Ustad Bismillah Khan, a legendary shehnai player, was not associated with the Maihar Gharana. He belonged to the Benares Gharana and was deeply rooted in the traditional folk and classical music of Benares (Varanasi). His work was central to the Ganga-Jamuni tehzeeb (syncretic culture) of the region. In contrast, Ali Akbar Khan (sarod player), Pt Ravi Shankar (sitar player), and Annapurna Devi (surbahar player) were all key figures associated with the Maihar Gharana, each contributing significantly to its development and popularity.

questions.question: What was Gandhiji’s age when he arrived in India in 1915 from South Africa, and led Indians in non-violent marches against racist restrictions?
questions.questionHtml: What was Gandhiji’s age when he arrived in India in 1915 from South Africa, and led Indians in non-violent marches against racist restrictions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 46 years.

Key Points

  • Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi, commonly known as Mahatma Gandhi, returned to India from South Africa in 1915.
  • At the time of his return, Gandhi was 46 years old.
  • He had spent 21 years in South Africa, from 1893 to 1914, fighting against racial discrimination.
  • Upon his return, Gandhi became a leading figure in the Indian struggle for independence, advocating for non-violent resistance and civil disobedience.
  • His leadership in India began with the Champaran and Kheda agitations of 1917 and 1918, respectively.
  • Gandhi's strategy of non-violent protest became a model for civil rights movements worldwide, earning him the title "The Father of the Nation" in India.

 Additional Information

  • South Africa
    • Gandhi's time in South Africa was crucial in the development of his political and ethical views, including the concept of Satyagraha, or truth force.
    • He initially went to South Africa to work as a lawyer before becoming a leader in the fight against unjust laws affecting the Indian diaspora there.
  • Non-violent resistance
    • Gandhi's philosophy of non-violent resistance inspired future civil rights movements, most notably the African-American civil rights movement led by Martin Luther King Jr. in the United States.
    • The principle of non-violence advocates for peaceful protest and civil disobedience as tools for achieving social and political change.

questions.question: Consider the following pairs: S. No. Reservoirs States 1. Balimela West Bengal 2. Tawa Madhya Pradesh 3. Stanley Tripura 4. Gobind Sagar Jammu and Kashmir How many pairs given above are not correctly matched?

S. No. Reservoirs States

3. Stanley Tripura
4. Gobind Sagar Jammu and Kashmir

questions.solution:

questions.question: Which indigenous system will India deploy to strengthen air defence over Delhi NCR against missiles, drones, and hostile aircraft?
questions.questionHtml: Which indigenous system will India deploy to strengthen air defence over Delhi NCR against missiles, drones, and hostile aircraft?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Integrated Air Defence Weapon System (IADWS).

In News

  • India is set to deploy an indigenous Integrated Air Defence Weapon System (IADWS) to protect Delhi NCR from missiles, drones, and hostile aircraft.

Key Points

  • IADWS integrates Quick Reaction Surface-to-Air Missiles (QRSAMs) and Very Short Range Air Defence Systems (VSHORADS) to counter diverse aerial threats.
  • It features advanced command-and-control networks for coordinated detection, tracking, and interception.
  • The system's deployment was accelerated after Pakistan’s attempted targeting during Operation Sindoor in May 2025.
  • The move marks a major policy shift as India dropped plans to procure the cost-intensive US-made NASAMS-II.

Additional Information

  • Components of IADWS
    • QRSAM: High-mobility missile system capable of rapidly engaging aircraft, missiles, and UAVs.
    • VSHORADS: Designed for very low-flying threats such as drones, helicopters, and slow aircraft.
    • Command-and-Control Network: Integrates sensors, radars, and shooters for real-time response.
  • Why the Deployment?
    • Triggered by Pakistan’s attempted strike during Operation Sindoor (May 2025).
    • Highlighted the urgency of strengthening Delhi NCR’s layered air defence grid.
    • Ensures faster reaction time and indigenous technological readiness.
  • Shift from NASAMS-II
    • India dropped plans to acquire NASAMS-II due to high procurement and lifecycle costs.
    • NASAMS-II is used to defend strategic US locations like Washington D.C. and the White House.
    • The shift reinforces India’s commitment to self-reliance and cost-effective defence solutions.
  • Roles of Agencies
    • Indian Air Force (IAF): Will operate the deployed air-defence system.
    • DRDO: Leads integration, testing, and system development.
    • Production Agencies: Support manufacturing, deployment, and lifecycle maintenance.

questions.question: Read the following statements about successor states of 18 th Century - (i) Bengal, Hyderabad and Avadhare considered as successor states. (ii) The founders of successor states never formally declared their independence from the Mughal empire. Choose the correct code -
questions.questionHtml:
Read the following statements about successor states of 18th Century -

(i) Bengal, Hyderabad and Avadhare considered as successor states.

(ii) The founders of successor states never formally declared their independence from the Mughal empire.

Choose the correct code -

options.text: Neither statement (i) nor statement (ii) is true
options.html: Neither statement (i) nor statement (ii) is true

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: 'Only statement (i) is true.'

Key Points

  • Bengal, Hyderabad, and Avadh are considered as successor states.
    • This statement is correct.
    • Successor states emerged in the 18th century as the Mughal Empire declined, marking a shift in power dynamics within the Indian subcontinent.
    • Bengal (under Murshid Quli Khan), Hyderabad (under Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah I), and Avadh (under Saadat Khan) were prominent successor states that emerged as semi-autonomous regions.
    • They were nominally under Mughal sovereignty but exercised de facto independence in administration, revenue, and military affairs.

Incorrect Statement

  • The founders of successor states never formally declared their independence from the Mughal Empire.
    • This statement is incorrect.
    • While the successor states initially maintained nominal allegiance to the Mughal Emperor, they often acted independently in practice.
    • Over time, these states gradually asserted their autonomy, and their rulers no longer sought formal recognition from the weakening Mughal authority.
    • Examples include the Nizam of Hyderabad establishing an independent administrative structure and the Nawabs of Bengal and Avadh managing their regions autonomously.

Hence, only statement (i) is true.

Additional Information

  • Successor States:
    • These states emerged during the disintegration of the Mughal Empire in the 18th century.
    • They are categorized into three types: successor states (e.g., Bengal, Hyderabad, Avadh), independent kingdoms (e.g., Mysore, Marathas), and foreign-influenced states (e.g., British-controlled areas).
  • Role of the Mughal Empire:
    • The Mughals continued to serve as a symbolic authority for some time, but their real power was limited to the region around Delhi.
    • This period marked the transition to regionalized governance and the eventual rise of colonial powers like the British.

questions.question: The rainfall occurring in equatorial regions is related to which of the following?
questions.questionHtml: The rainfall occurring in equatorial regions is related to which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Conventional Rainfall. Key Points

  • Convectional rainfall occurs in the Equatorial region.
  • The Equatorial region receives a greater amount of solar radiation.
  • When the energy of the sun heats up the earth's surface, there is an evaporation of water, forming water vapor. The warm air above the land surface expands and rises.
  • The rising warm air cools and condenses, forming cumulus clouds. This results in a rainfall known as convectional rainfall.
  • The abundant supply of moisture in the air, which provides high humidity, is another reason for the convectional rainfall.
  • convectional rainfall is common in areas including the Tropics that receive more heat. The Amazon rainforests receive convectional rainfall.

Additional Information

  • Cyclonic rainfall is provided by the cyclones created in tropical and temperate regions along the air mass fronts, where warm and cold air meet together 
  • Mountain Rain or Orographic rainfall is precipitation produced when the mountains of uplands act as barriers to airflow, forcing the air to rise and the moist air moving upslope to cool down by producing clouds and precipitation.
  • A monsoon is traditionally a seasonal reversing wind accompanied by corresponding changes in precipitation but is now used to describe seasonal changes in atmospheric circulation and precipitation.

Thus, rainfall occurring in equatorial regions is Conventional.

On the basis of highest population growth rate (Census, 2011), select the option that arranges the following states in descending order.

A) Bihar

B) Arunachal Pradesh

C) Meghalaya
questions.solution: The correct arrangement is Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh, Bihar, based on descending population growth rates from Census 2011. Meghalaya led with the highest growth rate, followed by Arunachal Pradesh, while Bihar had the lowest among the three.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding landforms? 1. Landforms take shape over millions of years and are influenced by environmental factors. 2. The type of landform influences the flora and fauna that can thrive in that region. 3. Human populations are evenly distributed across all landforms. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding landforms?

1. Landforms take shape over millions of years and are influenced by environmental factors.

2. The type of landform influences the flora and fauna that can thrive in that region.

3. Human populations are evenly distributed across all landforms.

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

Key Points

  • Landforms take shape over millions of years and are influenced by environmental factors. Processes like erosion, weathering, and tectonic activity shape landforms over long periods. Hence, statement 1 is correct.
  • The type of landform influences the flora and fauna that can thrive in that region. Different landforms support specific ecosystems and biodiversity. Hence, statement 2 is correct.
  • Human populations are not evenly distributed; they tend to concentrate in areas with favorable living conditions, like plains. Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.

questions.question: A concave mirror with a focal length of f is cut into two equal halves along its principal axis. What will be the focal length of each half?
questions.questionHtml: A concave mirror with a focal length of f is cut into two equal halves along its principal axis. What will be the focal length of each half?
questions.solution: When a concave mirror is cut into two equal halves along its principal axis, the focal length of each half remains the same, f. The focal length is a property of the mirror's curvature and does not change when the mirror is divided.
